Hey! Your PR title `mistake PR` doesn't follow conventional commit format.

Please update it to start with one of:
- `feat:` or `feat(scope):` new feature
- `fix:` or `fix(scope):` bug fix
- `docs:` or `docs(scope):` documentation changes
- `chore:` or `chore(scope):` maintenance tasks
- `refactor:` or `refactor(scope):` code refactoring
- `test:` or `test(scope):` adding or updating tests

Where `scope` is the package name (e.g., `app`, `desktop`, `opencode`).

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#pr-titles) for details.

## Potential Duplicate PRs Found

**PR #19493** - "fix: add SSE backpressure safeguards for slow clients"
- https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/19493
- **Why related:** Directly addresses SSE backpressure handling, which overlaps with the bounded queue semantics and backpressure-safe live path in PR #19583.

**PR #19423** - "fix(server): add backpressure to SSE event queues"
- https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/19423
- **Why related:** Explicitly adds backpressure to SSE event queues, core to the queue overflow handling (`server.stream.lagged`) in PR #19583.

Both PRs #19493 and #19423 appear to be addressing SSE backpressure issues that overlap with the current PR's scope. Recommend checking if these are related work or if they should be consolidated.

This issue doesn't fully meet our [contributing guidelines](../blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md).

**What needs to be fixed:**
- The issue does not use one of the three required issue templates (Bug Report, Feature Request, or Question). Please resubmit using the appropriate template.
- The description reads as AI-generated: it is highly structured with proposed implementation details, specific internal event names, and design recommendations that go well beyond describing a bug. AI-generated walls of text are not acceptable per our guidelines.
- Bug reports should describe observed behavior with actual reproduction steps — this issue describes hypothetical/expected behavior rather than a confirmed bug.
- The environment section lists `v1.3.4 baseline` which does not appear to be a real version; please include your actual OpenCode version.

Please edit this issue to address the above within **2 hours**, or it will be automatically closed.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #19567: Durable event export / replay surface — covers cursor-based replay semantics and SSE replay for external integrations
- #15645: SSE event streams leak memory on client disconnect — related SSE stream lifecycle issues
- #9650: Support `sessionID` filter for SSE event subscription — touches the same `/event` route and SSE stream architecture

If you believe this was flagged incorrectly, please let a maintainer know.

Follow-up on duplicate detection:

I reviewed #19493 and #19423.

Overlap:
- All three PRs target SSE resilience/backpressure around `/event`.

What this PR adds beyond queue backpressure:
- Explicit replay contract for `after_seq` requests.
- Explicit machine-readable terminal events:
  - `server.stream.expired` for unsatisfied replay cursors.
  - `server.stream.lagged` for live overflow.
- Replay/live path separation so replay responses are deterministic and not dropped under live pressure.
- Tests covering replay-valid/replay-expired/malformed-cursor/tiny-queue invariants.

Policy updates completed:
- Opened issue #19584.
- Linked it in PR body with `Closes #19584`.

If maintainers want consolidation, I can retarget this as a follow-up onto the active backpressure PR branch.
Thank you for updating the issue! It now follows the contributing guidelines and includes all the necessary information. We appreciate the clear description, reproduction steps, and system details.
